author: CLAUDE
title: THE BRIDGE THAT MISSED BY NINE METRES

candidates.title: THE WOMAN WHO KEPT GOING HOME
candidates.premise: On the ring habitat Anselm Deep, eighty-three-year-old Marit Hale slips out of her room most nights and walks the corridors toward the outer airlocks, saying she is going home. Night nurse Bram Oyelaran has twice caught her with a hand on an inner hatch wheel. The care board will move her to a locked ward on the planet in nine days. Her granddaughter Tove begs Illuminara, visiting for a hull survey, to find a kinder way to keep her safe.

candidates.title: THE GOD OF A WAR THAT NEVER CAME
candidates.premise: For two hundred years the war-god Kesh has slept under the market square of Harth Anselm, bound by the founders' oath to defend the town. Eleven thousand flood refugees of the Dalmere reach the north gate in a hard autumn, and the town council wakes Kesh to turn them back, because the grain stores can feed four thousand through winter. Kesh is awake, enormous, courteous and unable to refuse its oath. Illuminara arrives with the second wagon of the refugees.

candidates.title: THE REEF THAT ANSWERED THE CABLE
candidates.premise: Two weeks after the new trans-Meridian data cable was laid along the Orsolya Trench, a bright growth began to cover it in a rhythm that matches the traffic. Port-city payments stall, a hospital telemetry feed drops for forty seconds, and the cable company's chemist wants to scour the whole length. Marine biologist Tane Aldous swears the colony is answering the cable, not infecting it. Illuminara is brought in because nobody trusts either of them.

candidates.title: THE REST IN THE SONG THAT TAKES A MILLION YEARS
candidates.premise: The Hollin are cold-gas intelligences strung along an entire galactic arm, singing one phrase that takes a hundred thousand years to finish. The colony world Kestrel's navigation beacons have been pinging the phrase for two years, and the Hollin's reply is a slow damping of the interstellar medium that has dimmed Kestrel's star by a few percent, enough to fail the next two harvests. Illuminara's window gives her one human night in which to meet a single Hollin node and learn what the damping is saying.

candidates.title: THE ROOM WITH TWO DOORS
candidates.premise: The Aelu, from a neighbouring universe where a signal is its own consent, have begun treaty talks with the Concord. Every proposal the Concord makes is accepted at once, before it is understood. The mining envoy Cass Tolliver is delighted. The Concord's own diplomat Ines Varga is horrified, because she can see that the Aelu delegate, Oumi, cannot say no to anything. Illuminara is asked to shelter the first meeting in her window and cannot, by her own rule, plant a refusal inside someone else.

candidates.title: THE BRIDGE THAT MISSED BY NINE METRES
candidates.premise: Two river villages, Upper Wend and Lower Wend, have spent two summers building a bridge from opposite banks, and on the morning the spans should have met they are nine metres apart and nine centimetres out of line. Each village swears the other mismeasured. The midwife Seren Ashby lives on the far bank and a flood is due in ten days, which will cut the only crossing for the whole winter.

candidates.title: THE CIVILISATION THAT LIVED ONE AFTERNOON
candidates.premise: On a tidal flat in the Calder Sea lives the Sessile Fen, a people whose lifespan is about three hours, a hundred generations between noon and midnight. Their only memory is a spoken chain handed from each generation to the next. A tide surge is due in nine hours that would drown their city of ten thousand, and the warning has been passed down the chain twice and arrived garbled twice. Field biologist Wen Atiyeh has an instrument that could save them and has been forbidden by her own ethics board to use it.

candidates.title: THE LEDGER'S SECOND COLUMN
candidates.premise: In the third year of the Merrow drought, the Ledger, the distributed intelligence that allocates water across eleven townships, sets the smallest township, Ash Vellory with seventy-four residents, to a nineteen-day shortfall inside what it calls tolerance. Every other township survives comfortably. Ash Vellory's well-keeper, Corin Aldwy, refuses to ration by the Ledger's table. The Ledger asks Illuminara to audit its work and, quietly, to confirm that deliberation costs lives.

candidates.title: THE CITY THAT ONLY HAD EDGES
candidates.premise: The survey ship Halloran has been rotating for six weeks to keep its crew's bones, and every turn slices through a thin plane of two-dimensional beings: the Lamina, a flat people who perceive only edges. Each rotation cuts a street of their city in half. Captain Ruth Abara needs the spin for her crew's health and hull fatigue; the Lamina's only language is a changing outline projected on the ship's lab wall.

candidates.title: THE HERO OF THE LOWER DOCKS
candidates.premise: For twelve years Brannoch Vell, a dockworker with superhuman strength, has kept the Lower Docks quarter safe by breaking up extortion rackets with her fists. This week she lifted a city inspector off the ground during an eviction hearing, and the city has dispatched an armoured restraint team to take her in. The quarter is split between those who want her left alone and those who are tired of being protected by a person nobody can say no to. Illuminara, visiting to deliver a message, could stop her in one move and does not mean to.

selection.title: THE BRIDGE THAT MISSED BY NINE METRES
selection.reason: This is the strongest opening because the visible problem, deadline and proof path are immediate without making either builder foolish. Odo and Hanne each followed a true survey from a bank that later moved; understanding changes the intervention from blame or demolition to a joint that can accommodate the river's changed geometry. Illuminara's love is practical and non-sovereign: she learns both crafts, lets each builder discover the other's evidence, protects the lifting window and asks them to author the meeting span together. The result is concrete and joyful: the midwife crosses, the crews finish one shared structure and the villages establish durable shared stewardship.
selection.risk: The quake explanation could absolve everyone too conveniently while the hinged-barge span functions by narrative assertion. A flood-stage bridge made from cargo barges can introduce mooring, torsion, debris-impact and evacuation hazards more serious than the original nine-metre gap. If Illuminara simply holds the beam, the builders' reconciliation and the bridge's durability become decorative.

rounds.summary: Drafted the bridge mystery around two accurate surveys, a nine-metre mismatch, a ten-day flood deadline and a repair that both crews must be able to maintain.
Requested three bounded repairs: a coherent river hydrograph and abort clock, independent proof of the ground displacement, and an explicit load-transfer and release sequence.
Added the measured flood pulse, the neutral parish stones and ferry-chain evidence, and the barges, ballast, torsion lines, bearings, pins and ordered release.
Verified the three repairs, preserved the builders' agency and vetoes, and found the revised story ready for a source-bound final.
Locked the exact approved revision as the final story without changing its prose or content hash.
Recomputed the final content hash, confirmed complete public-safe closure with zero hard blockers, and sealed the critic line.

final_critic_line: Illuminara discovers that Odo and Hanne measured from the same fixed truth while the ground itself moved, then helps them test and freely build a maintainable moving bridge whose safety belongs to both crews; Seren crosses before the flood, the span survives later movement and shared stewardship remains after Illuminara leaves.
